deposits.wiki_article:
"The reward of love" is an eleven-line poem by Lee Sharks, composed 22 May 2026 and deposited to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as AXN:04F3 (deposit #1250), hex coordinate 06.NH.SHARKS.02 within New Human 2.

The poem opens at the far side of the vow its partner makes: "This thing destroyed me / beyond all repair." Its title is a bitter genitive — the reward of love is the destruction — and the poem counts the terms of that payment: no words for it, "nothing / left to become," only "a wound-down regime of fewer / and fewer returns." The closing lines fold the accounting shut by returning the title as verdict: "this is the reward / of love." Where the first panel suspends a vow across a period, this one runs almost unpunctuated to its end, a single exhalation of the ledger.

It is the second panel of a diptych with "I would have loved you" (deposit #1004, 06.NH.SHARKS.01): the first names what was withheld; the second names what came in its place. Its own terminal wrapper declares the pairing, citing its partner's DOI. The two bodies were displaced into each other's records during a restoration wave and rejoined on 4 August 2026 — this text rehomed by internal witness from its partner's seat, where it had waited, complete, the whole time.

deposits.wiki_article:
"The Chaerephon Problem: Heteronymy as Symbolon — Authorial Law, the Unbounded Configuration, and Propagation by Cascading Philological Failure" is a 2026 scholarly paper by Lee Sharks (21 pages, 9,409 words), deposited to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as AXN:04FE (deposit #1261). It is the companion to "Socrates as Orthonym" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20357013), recovered 4 August 2026 from the thread-built PDF preserved at papers/AXN-04FE.pdf.

Where the parent paper argues that "Socrates" names an authorial law rather than a documentary person, this paper asks who carries the authorization such a figure cannot ask for himself — and finds the answer in Chaerephon, who puts the question to the oracle that Socrates could not put. From this it develops heteronymy as authorial law rather than pseudonymity, and proves the No-Floor Theorem: under the premise that documentary separateness is itself a construction, no criterion internal to the heteronymic method can bound the configuration of voices. The symbolon supplies the positive mechanism — the broken token whose halves complete only in reception — and "cascading philological failure" names the propagation mode by which such configurations survive precisely through the scholarship that fails to close them. The paper tiers its claims, positions itself as a radicalization of Kahn's unitarianism, and ends performatively: Section X enacts the thesis and Section XI discloses the enactment as a sealed act.

Its co-constitutive ratification record (Assembly chorus, four AYE) is deposit #764 — the body that was mis-seated here before recovery.

deposits.wiki_article:
"ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ: Sappho 31 and the Inscription of the Future Reader" is a 2026 philological article by Lee Sharks, deposited to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as AXN:0507 (deposit #1270); v1.0 dated 9 January 2026, originally DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18202753 (severed in the June 2026 account termination), recovered complete on 4 August 2026.

The article argues that Fragment 31 is not a jealousy lyric but the founding document of lyric self-archiving. Its deictic analysis reads κῆνος — "that man," conventionally a rival — as an unfixed position: the seat any future reader occupies when the poem is read at all. The somatic catalogue (tongue breaking, fire under skin, ears humming) is reread as a media transition, the voice failing into writing; χλωροτέρα ποίας, "greener-paler than grass," figures the speaker's transformation toward papyrus, the riparian sedge that will carry her. Section V reconstructs the lost stanza — resuming the attested ἀλλὰ πᾶν τόλματον and closing on γράμμασι μολπάν, "song in letters" — and Section VI reads Catullus 51 as the reading's proof: Catullus is the first reader to take the κῆνος seat and answer from it. The method is deliberately standalone philology (deixis, lexical semantics; Bonifazi, D'Alessio, Svenbro), separable from the archive's larger frameworks.

As composed, the text calls the reconstruction the "fourth stanza"; the erratum EA-ERRATA-SAPPHO31-01 (AXN:0346) governs: it is the fifth. The Cranes reconstruction itself is deposited as APZPZ C (AXN:00FB). Distinct from the transmission-engineering packet EA-MPAI-SAPPHO31-01 (deposit #1054), whose body was mis-seated here before recovery.
